title: Archibald Glasgow of Leith: shoemaker and maltman identity test
question: Can Archibald Glasgow, son of William Glasgow the Leith mealmaker and documented as a shoemaker in 1647, be identified as Archibald Glasgow, maltman and indweller in Leith, whose 1662 testament names Agnes Watson and sons Archibald, George, and William?
conclusion: The identity remains unresolved. The 1639 apprenticeship, William Glasgow's 1646 testament, and the 1647 retour securely identify one Archibald Glasgow of Leith as William's son and a shoemaker. The 1662 original testament securely identifies an Archibald Glasgow of Leith as a maltman, husband of Agnes Watson, and father of Archibald, George, and William, but it gives no parentage, former occupation, guild status, property history, or other statement connecting him to William's son. The uncommon name, same town, and compatible chronology make identity possible, but they do not overcome the explicit occupational discontinuity. No marriage, child baptism, deed, property record, or guild record bridging the two descriptions was found in this bounded pass; a change from shoemaker to maltman must not be assumed.

findings.claim: On 23 October 1639 Archibald Glasgow, son of William Glasgow, mealmaker in Leith, was entered as apprentice to Thomas Park, cordiner.
findings.basis: A digitized scan of the printed apprentice-register transcript reads: "Glasgow, Archibald, son to William G., mealmaker in Leith, with Thomas Park, cordiner." This is a derivative printed transcript of the burgh record, not the original minute.
findings.source_reference: Francis J. Grant, ed., The Register of Apprentices of the City of Edinburgh, 1583-1666, Scottish Record Society 28 (1906), p. 71, entry dated 23 October 1639

findings.claim: William Glasgow's testament connects the 1639 apprentice's stated father to an Archibald Glasgow who was William's lawful son and sole executor.
findings.basis: The original commissary-court scan describes William Glasgow as a mealmaker and indweller in Leith and records Archibald Glasgow as his lawful son and only executor dative. It supplies no occupation for Archibald, so it supports the father-son chain but does not bridge the later trades.
findings.source_reference: National Records of Scotland, Edinburgh Commissary Court, testament dative of William Glasgow, CC8/8/62, images 461-462; death September 1644, confirmation 1646

findings.claim: On 1 May 1647 Archibald Glasgow, shoemaker and inhabitant of Leith, was retoured heir of William Glasgow, mealmaker and inhabitant there, his father.
findings.basis: The digitized scan of the printed official retour abstract reads: "ARCHIBALDUS GLASGOW, calcearius incola villæ de Leith, heres Willielmi Glasgow farinarii incolæ dictæ villæ, patris." Calcearius identifies Archibald as a shoemaker. This is a published abstract referencing, but not itself reproducing, original retour xix.128.
findings.source_reference: Inquisitionum ad Capellam Domini Regis Retornatarum, quae in Publicis Archivis Scotiae adhuc servantur, Abbreviatio, vol. 2, General Retour no. 3278, 1 May 1647; original xix.128

findings.claim: The 1662 testament belongs to Archibald Glasgow, maltman and indweller in Leith, and names Agnes Watson and lawful sons Archibald, George, and William.
findings.basis: The original commissary-court scan opens with "Archibald Glasgow maltman Indweller In leith". It identifies Agnes Watson as his spouse/relict and tutor and Archibald, George, and William as his lawful sons and sole executors. The record does not name his father and does not call him a shoemaker, cordiner, or former shoemaker.
findings.source_reference: National Records of Scotland, Edinburgh Commissary Court, testament of Archibald Glasgow, CC8/8/70, images 689-693, 1662

findings.claim: No source found in this pass bridges the shoemaker documented in 1647 to the maltman documented in 1662.
findings.basis: The local dossier and cached record corpus contain the two endpoint descriptions but no marriage, baptism, sasine, deed, guild entry, or property statement using both occupations or supplying the 1662 man's parentage. Targeted exact-name, spouse, child-mother, trade, and NRS catalogue searches returned no relevant historical record. This is a bounded negative result, not proof that no bridge exists.
findings.source_reference: Local Glasgow-3078 evidence dossier plus targeted searches recorded below, reviewed 10 September 2026

findings.claim: The current association of the 1662 maltman testament with WikiTree profile Glasgow-3078 is not independently proved by the records examined.
findings.basis: Same uncommon name, Leith residence, and a fifteen-year interval are compatible with one man, but the only explicit occupations differ: shoemaker in 1647 and maltman in 1662. The 1662 record lacks the father William or another unique identifier, and cached profile data only repeats the attachment rather than supplying a primary bridge.
findings.source_reference: Cached WikiTree profile narrative compared with General Retour 3278 and NRS CC8/8/70

searches.target: Unread local Glasgow-3078 dossier, profile cache, and research plan
searches.result: Found a secure 1639-1647 father-son and shoemaker chain and the separately described 1662 maltman family, but no bridging record. The profile attachment is derivative and does not resolve the conflict.

searches.target: Cached repository records for exact Archibald Glasgow/Agnes Watson combinations, children Archibald, George, and William, and shoemaker/maltman role overlap
searches.result: No independent marriage, baptism, guild, deed, sasine, or property record bridging the identities was located.

searches.target: Exact web searches for Archibald Glasgow with Agnes Watson or Watsone in Leith
searches.result: No relevant historical result; returned results were unrelated people or later periods. Failed search, not negative proof.

searches.target: Exact and variant web searches combining Archibald Glasgow with shoemaker, cordiner, maltman, or Thomas Park
searches.result: No source spanning the occupations was returned. Failed search, not negative proof.

searches.target: Indexed web searches for George Glasgow or William Glasgow with mother Agnes Watson in Leith
searches.result: No relevant baptism or family index entry was returned. Failed search, not negative proof.

searches.target: National Records of Scotland online-catalogue web index for exact Archibald Glasgow in Leith
searches.result: No relevant catalogue item was returned; visible hits were unrelated records. This does not search unindexed record contents.

searches.target: Internet Archive scan of the printed Edinburgh apprentice register
searches.result: The known volume and page citation are preserved in the local dossier; direct browser retrieval returned an internal error in this pass. It remains a digitized derivative transcript rather than the original burgh minute.

searches.target: Internet Archive scan of the printed retour abstracts
searches.result: The known volume, retour number, date, and exact Latin abstract are preserved in the local dossier; direct browser retrieval returned an internal error in this pass. It remains an official published abstract rather than original retour xix.128.

next_record: Inspect the original South Leith parish-register images, NRS OPR 692/2, for an Archibald Glasgow-Agnes Watson marriage and baptisms of sons Archibald, George, and William, then inspect any matching entry's witnesses and occupational wording. A contemporaneous entry naming William the mealmaker as grandfather, Thomas Park as associate, or Archibald under both shoemaker/cordiner and maltman descriptions would provide the needed bridge; a bare name match would not.
